location.scope: Bali-wide; verify local and site-specific rules

content.definition: Visitors are expected to behave respectfully in public settings including roads, restaurants, shopping centers, attractions, and shared community spaces.
content.cultural_context: Bali Governor Circular Letter No. 07 of 2025 requires respectful behavior in sacred areas, attractions, restaurants, shopping centers, roads, and other public places. It prohibits profane language, disrespectful behavior, disturbances, and aggressive conduct toward officials, local communities, or fellow tourists.
content.significance: Public conduct affects residents, workers, other visitors, and shared use of public space.
common_situations: Speaking with residents or service workers
Posting content about local people online

do: Speak politely and remain calm when resolving disagreements
Respect residents, workers, officials, and other visitors
Follow posted instructions and directions from authorized personnel
dont: Use abusive or threatening language
Harass or intimidate others
Create disturbances or act aggressively in public

common_misconceptions: Being on holiday does not exempt visitors from Indonesian law.
Not every disagreement is automatically a legal offence.
regional_variations: Specific conduct rules may apply at particular attractions, businesses, ceremonies, or customary village areas.
content.additional_notes: Distinguish the circular's requirements from general etiquette. Do not infer penalties; refer to current law and competent authorities.

content.definition: Visitors should keep public spaces and natural environments clean, dispose of waste appropriately, and follow applicable restrictions on single-use plastics.
content.cultural_context: The 2025 Bali Governor Circular prohibits littering or polluting lakes, springs, rivers, seas, and public areas. It also lists plastic bags, Styrofoam, plastic straws, and plastic beverage containers among prohibited single-use plastics for foreign tourists.
content.significance: The guidance applies beyond beaches and attractions to public areas and waterways.
common_situations: Eating or drinking at beaches and public spaces
Visiting rivers, lakes, springs, or coastal areas

do: Use designated waste bins or take waste with you when bins are unavailable
Keep waste away from waterways and beaches
Ask vendors about reusable alternatives
dont: Drop litter in streets, beaches, rivers, lakes, springs, or the sea
Use the specific single-use plastic items prohibited by applicable Bali rules

common_misconceptions: The circular addresses both littering and specified single-use plastic products.
regional_variations: Implementation and waste facilities may differ by location; check local signage and current rules.
content.additional_notes: Do not broaden the exact list of prohibited products without checking the current regulation.

content.definition: Visitors should dress appropriately for the setting and avoid photography or public behavior that disrespects people, ceremonies, sacred places, or religious symbols.
content.cultural_context: The 2025 Governor Circular asks foreign tourists to dress modestly and respectfully in sacred areas, attractions, public places, and activities in Bali. It prohibits indecent or inappropriate photographs, including nudity, when these desecrate sacred places, temples, sacred objects, or religious symbols.
content.significance: Clothing and photography can affect dignity, privacy, and the sanctity of a place or event.
common_situations: Taking photos of residents or performers
Visiting public attractions or sacred sites

do: Dress respectfully and follow venue-specific clothing requirements
Ask permission before close-up portraits of identifiable people
Follow photography signs and organizer instructions
dont: Take or publish indecent or nude photographs at sacred places
Ignore venue or ceremony restrictions
Assume public access means unrestricted photography

common_misconceptions: The circular's dress guidance does not mean every venue has the same dress code.
Photography rules may vary by location and event.
regional_variations: Temples, ceremonies, private businesses, and public events may each have their own requirements.
content.additional_notes: Consent for portraits is a courtesy recommendation; the circular specifically addresses respectful dress and indecent photography at sacred places.

title: Driving Eligibility and Legal Vehicle Use

location.scope: Bali-wide; verify local and site-specific rules

content.definition: Anyone driving in Bali must comply with Indonesian driving-licence requirements and use a legally operated vehicle appropriate for the journey.
content.cultural_context: The 2025 Governor Circular requires foreign tourists operating vehicles to hold a valid national or international driving licence and use four-wheeled transport from legally registered rental businesses or associations. Kejati Bali's FAQ summarizes licence and vehicle-document expectations.
content.significance: A valid licence and legally operated vehicle help ensure drivers are authorized and vehicles can be identified by authorities.
common_situations: Being stopped at a traffic checkpoint

do: Confirm your licence is valid for the vehicle class and recognized in Indonesia
Carry required driving and vehicle documents
Use a properly registered rental provider and check roadworthiness
dont: Drive without the required valid licence
Assume a home-country licence alone is sufficient
Use a rental vehicle when its legal status is unclear

common_misconceptions: Renting a scooter does not itself authorize someone to ride it.
regional_variations: Underlying driving rules are national; the Bali circular reiterates obligations for foreign tourists.
content.additional_notes: For legal questions, refer users to Indonesian Police or the relevant licensing authority. Do not make individualized legal determinations.

title: Basic Road Safety and Traffic Compliance

location.scope: Bali-wide; verify local and site-specific rules

content.definition: Road users must obey signs and directions, use required safety equipment, respect passenger limits, and avoid impaired or distracted driving.
content.cultural_context: The 2025 circular requires valid licences, compliance with traffic rules, helmets, obedience to signs, passenger limits, and no driving under the influence of alcohol or illegal drugs. Bali Police have highlighted helmet and seatbelt use, phone use while driving, wrong-way driving, underage riding, and overloading as enforcement concerns.
content.significance: Road safety protects drivers, passengers, pedestrians, cyclists, and other road users.
common_situations: Riding a scooter with a passenger

do: Wear a properly fastened motorcycle helmet
Use seat belts
Follow signs, signals, and police directions
Stay within passenger capacity
Stop safely before using a phone
Never drive under the influence
dont: Ride without a helmet
Use a mobile phone while driving
Drive against traffic
Overload a vehicle
Drive if underage or not legally licensed

common_misconceptions: A short ride or quiet road does not make safety requirements optional.
A rental provider handing over a vehicle does not transfer responsibility for safe driving.
regional_variations: Traffic density and road conditions vary; follow current signs and police directions.
content.additional_notes: Police reporting identifies enforcement priorities, not a complete list of offences or penalties.

title: Road Position, Parking, Pedestrians, and Accident Response

location.scope: Bali-wide; verify local and site-specific rules

content.definition: Drivers should use the correct side of the road, signal and maneuver carefully, avoid obstructing traffic, respect pedestrians and cyclists, and respond responsibly after accidents.
content.cultural_context: Kejati Bali's foreigner legal FAQ summarizes left-side driving, signaling before turns, avoiding mobile phone use, and respecting pedestrian and traffic rules. The 2025 Governor Circular requires compliance with Indonesian traffic regulations and signs.
content.significance: Predictable driving and consideration for vulnerable road users reduce conflict, especially on narrow or crowded roads.
common_situations: Joining traffic from a side road
Being involved in a road accident

do: Drive on the left
Signal before turning or changing direction
Park only where permitted and do not block traffic or pedestrian paths
Give pedestrians and cyclists space
If an accident occurs, stop, assist where safe, and contact police or emergency services when required
dont: Drive against traffic
Park where restricted or obstructive
Use a phone while driving
Leave an accident scene without following legal duties

common_misconceptions: Road etiquette is also about predictable behavior and consideration, not only avoiding fines.
regional_variations: Road layouts and parking controls differ by locality; follow signs, markings, and police directions.
content.additional_notes: The Kejati FAQ is explanatory information, not a substitute for current statutory text. Accident procedures need direct current legal/police confirmation.
